work.title: 大秦景教宣元至本經 (Book of the Origin of Origins), Luoyang pillar
work.edition: Machine translation (claude-opus-5-5, Patristica, 2026-11-13) of: Chinese Wikisource, «大秦景教宣元至本經», revision 517908 (2016-09-26); the text of the Luoyang sutra pillar (經幢, dated 元和九年十二月 = 814/815, excavated 2006) and the pillar's dedication (幢記); …… and □ mark damaged text. The page's other witnesses are not included: the Dunhuang manuscript (Li Shengduo's 宣元本經) and Kojima manuscript B, a modern forgery (Lin Wushu). Listed in the Zunjing among the books Jingjing translated.

paragraphs.text: Pillar inscription: The Book of the Luminous Teaching of Daqin on Proclaiming the Origin and Reaching the Root (twelfth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe in the Tang [AD 814]; the pillar was excavated in 2006 in the eastern suburbs of Luoyang)

At that time the Luminous, All-Pervading Lord of the Law was in the city of Nazareth in the land of Daqin, upon the precious cloud-throne of the Law in the Palace of Harmonious Light. He meant to settle the question of the true origin with those who held the two views. All who responded with joy came, gathering like clouds from the seven directions. There were all the bright and pure ones, all the divine heavens, lords of the Law of equal wonder, countless hosts of the enlightened, and the peoples who held the three hundred and sixty-five different views. Such beings, without bound or limit, lamented their own emptiness and darkness, for they had long lost the true origin. They all gathered in the Palace of Light and looked up to him with one heart in utmost reverence. Then the Luminous, All-Pervading Lord of the Law, upright and solemn, advanced in thought. He looked up to the Sovereign of Emptiness, personally received his sealed decree, and said to the assembly: "Welcome, assembly of the Law! The truest arrival is a coming from nowhere. Now you may pass into the Constant, open the way to life and put an end to death. Let each of you fulfil his portion and quietly contemplate my teaching. If you understand the Originless, your obstacles will scatter." Then he proclaimed the true and constant decree of the Artisan Emperor of Mysterious Transformation: "Without origin, without words, without a way, without conditions; wondrous being, non-being; deep, still, ever thus. I have heard that the great Alaha opened from nothing and opened forth difference. He brought things to birth without the stirring of mind [?]; he hid his transforming work, and it was spontaneous. From primal unity he issued forth, yet did not issue forth. Without nature, without motion, spiritual and void, he set in emptiness the pivot and axle of causes and conditions. Nature he established as the root of forms; causes and conditions he assigned as the vehicle of response. He divided and ordered the teeming array, the three births and the seven ranks. He spread out all names and numbers, which had no power to sustain themselves; he made each complete the others, taught them understanding, and had them return to the original true substance. Now he crafts without making. In answer to his decree things come to completion in obedience; they change without delay. By joining nothing he makes being; by breaking being he makes nothing. Everything created and transformed depends on him. Therefore he is called the Artisan Emperor of Mysterious Transformation, the Imperceptible Sovereign of Emptiness. Hidden and manifest, he answers the living who call on him. How wondrous are his spiritual heirs, who reverently look up to the Creator! Those deluded about the original Artisan King do not yet understand that Alaha never flaunts his works and claims no kindness for his gifts. He embraces the vast and discerns the minute, and nurtures all beings as one. He regards everything that flows into being as a single mote of dust, and even that mote is not dust. He sees without seeing, because he sees all seeing. Boundless, he hears without hearing, because he hears all hearing. Boundless, he is without force, because he upholds all force. Boundless, he turns toward nothing [?]; he is without image and without law. What he beholds has no bound and no edge; he alone is self-existent. He governs well without fixed method; his steadfast seat has no limit; his wondrous rule reaches everywhere, and all things and forms take him as their pattern. Only spiritual beings respond in different ways, and as their darkness builds up they lose the way. Therefore he teaches them with goodness, governs them with fairness, and saves them with mercy. Whoever knows to change will have every sin forgiven. This means that the Artisan Emperor can accomplish every transformation, yet he himself is not produced by transformation, and what is transformed passes away in the end. Only the Artisan Emperor neither wanes nor waxes, is neither muddy nor clear; he keeps hold of the true emptiness, ever existing and unchanging [?]

Because the Messiah responds to the great blessing of the original spirit, wisdom awakens fully to it: emptiness and being are not empty; without [?], it does not stagnate in emptiness [?] the body of the Spirit (Luhena), ultimately true and still, the ever-joyful life. Thus we know that the Artisan Emperor, being without bounds, does not pursue [?] numbers, and awakens people to the great awakening [?]. Those who understand all gain benefit [?] people stagnate in consciousness; this view will go astray, for the spirit is originally undivided [?] and yet it bears with them; once understood, it finally passes away. Because hearing is the master, they pass into the spirit and subdue consciousness, and do not follow consciousness in its shifting [?] below, fully provided with the eight realms; by hearing they bring forth the three constants; the crossing of the eight realms that extinguishes death; long examining themselves and deeply repenting, watchful and careful [?] When the Luminous, All-Pervading Lord of the Law had finished speaking, he looked over the assembly in its awakening, and in that gathering he expounded with wisdom [?] all realms. If anyone receives and keeps this, reads and recites it, believes and understands it, and diligently practises it, know that this person [?] as when the sea overflows and the hollows are levelled, as when the sun rises and darkness is extinguished. Each attains the great stillness, understands the self-existent Constant, and rejoices, cleansed [?]
Record of the Pillar of the Book of the Luminous Teaching of Daqin on Proclaiming the Origin and Reaching the Root

Now the Most Holy appears in response to need, and his benefits spread everywhere without limit. Our Originless True Lord, the Artisan Emperor [?] the sea, and nourishes every kind of creature. The sun and moon shine, the five planets move in their courses, then [?] those who are scattered and perish in the end, passing into the spirit and subduing consciousness, understanding and gathering without omission, all pass beyond [?] the sea. Deep and dark, the Way cannot be named; the Master did not speak of it; the world cannot [?] it; good [?] the realm of the beginningless and of the future: this is our Artisan Emperor Alaha. [?] All who can chant and keep it receive luminous blessing, and how much more when it is written on an inscribed pillar [?]. I inherited the family as the heir of the main line. I regret that before I could show my filial devotion I was suddenly bereft of my parents' instruction; of the high hall [?] deeply moved by the causes of things, with humble feelings and a heart like tangled weeds, I erected this pillar and record, engraving the scripture and carving the stone, in order to [?] comfort the spirit path of my late mother, the Grand Lady An of the state of An, and of my late master-uncle He [?]. May the luminous sun hang long, shining brightly on the dark realm, so that the true nature does not go astray; this is the luminous nature. Now, seeking [?] the departed souls now present; the relatives also pray to be free of all obstacles and hardships, with lives as long as pine and bamboo, old and young [?] in their proper order. The grounds for establishing the grave and buying the burial plot: it falls under Bairen [?] in Gande township, Luoyang county [?] the beginning: on the eighth day of the twelfth month of the ninth year of Yuanhe it was bought from Cui Xingben, with guarantor [?] relatives, who will make seasonal offerings and libations, with heaven and earth as joint witnesses. We bought stone from the Southern Mountain, polished it to a lustrous clarity, and engraved the scripture at the tomb. I, Wenyi, ashamed of my own clumsiness, took up the brush and composed this text; may gentlemen of the future not laugh at it. At that time [?] by imperial appointment: guard officer of the Right Yulin Army at the Eastern Capital, Peirong Commandant, acting [?] of the Liangchuan garrison in Ruzhou under the Left Weiwei Guard [?]. The relatives on both sides of the family inscribe their names as follows. Younger brother, the Luminous monk Qingsu; elder cousin Shaocheng; maternal uncle An Shaolian [?]; adoptive uncle, unassigned general of the Left Longwu Army at the Upper Capital, concurrently guard officer, General Ningyuan, acting Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard, appointed with the status of a regular official [?]. Abbot of the Daqin Monastery, Fahe Xuanying, of the secular surname Mi; the Venerable Master of Rites Xuanqing, of the secular surname Mi; the Venerable of the Nine Grades Zhitong, of the secular surname Kang. Chang'er, the household servant who oversees the grave and the estate. Therefore this record is inscribed.
